items.name: Spec Compliance
items.note: The diff retains the original one-derivation/one-insert end state and implements only the operator-authorized Windows PID repair plus its evidence.

items.name: Error Handling
items.note: OpenProcess denial is handled conservatively, failed waits do not prove liveness, invalid DWORD values are rejected, and every opened handle closes in finally.

items.name: Security Basics
items.note: No input is executed or interpolated into a shell; the PID is range-checked before crossing the Win32 boundary and no secrets enter the diff.

items.name: Test Quality
items.note: Outcome tests cover no-signal dispatch, running/terminated/failed wait states, access denial, invalid and oversized PIDs, handle closure, and the native current-process path.

items.name: Performance Basics
items.note: The Windows path performs one handle open, one zero-timeout wait, and one close; POSIX cost is unchanged.

items.name: Naming & Structure
items.note: The private helper and constants follow existing module conventions; Ruff is clean and no file-size ratchet is introduced by the PID follow-up.

items.name: Affected Boundaries
items.note: No serialized format changes; pids.json remains an existing consumer input and the added process query changes only runtime interpretation.

items.name: Test Hygiene Probe
items.note: scan_test_hygiene.py --diff reports no findings; the platform behavior is covered without collection-time skips.
